statement: You are given two strings s and t.

They are isomorphic when the characters of s can be replaced to produce t, under one fixed rule: every occurrence of a character is replaced by the same character, and two different characters are never replaced by the same character. A character may be replaced by itself.
Return true if s and t are isomorphic, and false otherwise.

examples.explanation: Replacing e with a and g with d turns "egg" into "add".
The two o's of s would have to become both a and r, which one fixed rule cannot do.
